spec.title: Deadlocks
spec.description: Transactions the deadlock detector aborted. The losing statement is in the server log.

spec.expr: topk(5, sum by (instance, datname) (pg_database_size_bytes{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}))

spec.title: Version rollout
spec.description: Servers running each version, stacked to the fleet total. A band only moves when a server is upgraded, so flat is the normal state.

spec.title: Sessions by database
spec.description: Backends connected to each database, running or not — the peak within each bucket, so the stacked total can exceed the backends alive at any one instant.

spec.title: Idle in transaction by server
spec.description: Peak backends inside a transaction but not executing in each bucket, `aborted` ones included. Sampled once a minute, so a shorter one can fall between scrapes.

spec.expr: max_over_time(sum by (instance) (pg_stat_activity_count{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*", state=~"idle in transaction.*"})[$__interval:]) > 0

spec.title: Closest to the connection limit
spec.description:
The peak each server reached against its own `max_connections`.
- Ignores the Database filter: the limit is server-wide.
- An exporter that serves several servers counts the backends of its first one, against the smallest `max_connections` among them.

spec.expr:
sort_desc(topk(3, max by (instance) (max_over_time((
  sum by (instance) (pg_stat_database_numbackends{instance=~"$instance"})
  /
  min by (instance) (pg_settings_max_connections{instance=~"$instance"})
)[$__range:5m]))))

spec.title: Longest transaction by database
spec.description: Longest transaction open at any point in each bucket, idle ones included. A gap is a bucket in which no database held one.

spec.title: Locks by mode
spec.description: Peak locks held in each bucket, across every server in scope. `accesssharelock` is an ordinary read; `accessexclusivelock` blocks everything else on the table and is the one that stalls traffic.

spec.title: Locks by database
spec.description: Peak locks held in each bucket.

spec.title: Rollback share by server
spec.description: Rollbacks as a share of all transactions. Frameworks that wrap read-only work in a transaction and abort it keep this high without anything being wrong.

spec.expr:
sum by (instance) (rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__rate_interval]))
/
(sum by (instance) (rate(pg_stat_database_xact_commit{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

spec.title: Rows written
spec.description: An update writes a new row version and leaves the old one for vacuum, so update-heavy load costs twice: once here and again as a dead row.

spec.title: Query time by server
spec.description: Seconds of statement execution per second — the number of backends busy on average. Above the core count the server is oversubscribed.

spec.title: Cache hit ratio by database
spec.description: A database idle in a bucket has no point there rather than a ratio of zero.

spec.expr:
sum by (instance, datname) (rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__rate_interval]))
/
(sum by (instance, datname) (rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(pg_stat_database_blks_read{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

spec.title: Buffer reads
spec.description: Blocks the backends read, scaled by the 8 KiB page size. `From disk` is a miss in shared buffers, which the operating system page cache may still have served, and has its own axis on the right.

spec.title: Block I/O time by server
spec.description: Milliseconds backends spent waiting on block I/O per second. Requires `track_io_timing`; a server with it off never appears here.

spec.title: Shared buffer allocation
spec.description: Rate at which backends claim shared buffers, scaled by the 8 KiB page size. Sustained allocation against a small `shared_buffers` means the working set does not fit.

spec.title: Table reads from disk
spec.description: Bytes read past shared buffers, heap and index blocks together, within the database each exporter connects to. The six heaviest.

spec.expr:
sum by (instance, relname) (increase(pg_statio_user_tables_heap_blocks_read{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__interval]) + increase(pg_statio_user_tables_idx_blocks_read{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__interval])) * 8192
and on (instance, relname)
topk(6, sum by (instance, relname) (increase(pg_statio_user_tables_heap_blocks_read{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__range] @ end()) + increase(pg_statio_user_tables_idx_blocks_read{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__range] @ end())))

spec.title: Dead rows by table
spec.description:
Row versions left behind by updates and deletes, waiting for vacuum; the six heaviest tables.
- A sawtooth is autovacuum keeping up; a ramp is not.

spec.title: Peak connection use
spec.description:
The busiest server's backends against its own `max_connections`.
- Ignores the Database filter: the limit is server-wide.
- An exporter that serves several servers counts the backends of its first one, against the smallest `max_connections` among them.

spec.title: Dead row share by table
spec.description: Dead rows against the whole table; the six heaviest tables, those under 1000 rows excluded.

spec.expr:
pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}
/
(pg_stat_user_tables_n_live_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} + pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 1000)
and on (instance, schemaname, relname)
topk(6, max_over_time((pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}
/
(pg_stat_user_tables_n_live_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} + pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 1000))[$__range:10m] @ end()))

spec.title: Vacuum and analyze runs
spec.description: Completed runs across the tables each exporter can see; a run counts once it finishes.

spec.title: Tables awaiting vacuum
spec.description:
Tables holding more than 100 dead rows, newest statistics.
- `Last autovacuum` is the age of the last automatic run; `never` means none since the statistics were reset.
- Table statistics reach only the database each exporter connects to.

spec.expr: sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 100)

sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}
/
(pg_stat_user_tables_n_live_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} + pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"})
and on (instance, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 100))

sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (time() - (pg_stat_user_tables_last_autovacuum{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 0)
and on (instance, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 100))

sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_mod_since_analyze{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}
and on (instance, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 100))

spec.title: Largest tables
spec.description:
Tables over 1 MiB.
- `Rows` is the planner's estimate of live rows.
- `Seq scans` counts full-table scans over the range.
- Table statistics reach only the database each exporter connects to.

spec.expr: sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 1048576)

sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_index_size_bytes{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}
and on (instance, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 1048576))

sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_live_tup{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}
and on (instance, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 1048576))

sum by (instance, datname, schemaname, relname) (increase(pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__range])
and on (instance, schemaname, relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"} > 1048576))

spec.title: Rows read by sequential scan
spec.description:
Rows walked by full-table scans, the six heaviest tables.
- Large and steady on a big table is a missing index; on a small one the planner is right to skip the index.

spec.expr:
sum by (instance, relname) (rate(pg_stat_user_tables_seq_tup_read{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__rate_interval]))
and on (instance, relname)
topk(6, sum by (instance, relname) (increase(pg_stat_user_tables_seq_tup_read{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__range] @ end())))

spec.title: Index scan share by server
spec.description: Scans that used an index, within the database each exporter connects to. Counts scans, not their cost, so a low share on a database of small tables is not a fault.

spec.expr:
sum by (instance) (increase(pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__interval]))
/
(sum by (instance) (increase(pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__interval]) + increase(pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__interval])) > 0)

spec.title: HOT update share by server
spec.description: Updates that fit in the same page and left the indexes alone, within the database each exporter connects to. A low share on update-heavy load means every update also writes to every index.

spec.expr:
sum by (instance) (increase(pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_hot_upd{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__interval]))
/
(sum by (instance) (increase(pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_upd{instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname", datname!~"template.*"}[$__interval])) > 0)

spec.title: Databases
spec.description: Sizes are current; growth, temporary files and bytes spilled are over the dashboard range.

spec.title: Database growth
spec.description: Change in size per bucket, negative after a vacuum or a drop; a database whose size did not change has no point.

spec.title: WAL against max_wal_size
spec.description:
Bytes in `pg_wal` against each server's own `max_wal_size`.
- Flat is normal: checkpoints recycle the segments.
- Sustained growth past 100 % means something is pinning them: a stalled replication slot or a failing archive command.
- An exporter that serves several servers reports the WAL of its first one, read against the smallest `max_wal_size` among them.

spec.title: Transactions
spec.description: Commits and rollbacks together.

spec.title: Checkpoints
spec.description: Checkpoints begun, from the server log. More than one per `checkpoint_timeout` is WAL volume triggering them, and argues for a larger `max_wal_size`.

spec.title: Checkpoint duration
spec.description: Longest checkpoint completed in each bucket, write and sync together. Approaching `checkpoint_timeout` means the next one starts before this one is spread out.

spec.expr: max by (host) (max_over_time({job="postgres", host=~"$instance"} |= `checkpoint complete` | regexp `total=(?P<total>[0-9.]+) s` | unwrap total [$__interval]))

spec.description:
Newest 1000 lines from the servers that write to `/var/log/postgresql`, coloured by the severity in the line.
- `Hide checkpoints` drops checkpoint chatter by default; Storage & WAL counts and times it.
- Servers that log elsewhere, such as to a container runtime, do not appear here.
- `LOG:  duration:` marks a statement over `log_min_duration_statement`.

spec.expr:
{job="postgres", host=~"$instance"} !~ `$hide_checkpoints`
  | regexp `\] (?:\S+ )?(?P<severity>PANIC|FATAL|ERROR|WARNING|NOTICE|LOG|DETAIL|STATEMENT|HINT):`
  | label_format level=`{{ if or (eq .severity "PANIC") (eq .severity "FATAL") }}critical{{ else if eq .severity "ERROR" }}error{{ else if eq .severity "WARNING" }}warn{{ else }}info{{ end }}`
  | drop app, detected_level, filename, job, service_name, severity

spec.title: Statistics & logging
spec.description: A server with `track_io_timing` off never appears in Block I/O time; one with `log_min_duration_statement` off never reaches the Server log with a slow query.

spec.expr:
sum by (level) (count_over_time(
  {job="postgres", host=~"$instance"} !~ `$hide_checkpoints`
  | regexp `\] (?:\S+ )?(?P<severity>PANIC|FATAL|ERROR|WARNING|NOTICE|LOG|DETAIL|STATEMENT|HINT):`
  | label_format level=`{{ if or (eq .severity "PANIC") (eq .severity "FATAL") }}critical{{ else if eq .severity "ERROR" }}error{{ else if eq .severity "WARNING" }}warn{{ else }}info{{ end }}`
[$__interval]))

spec.title: Longest transaction
spec.description: Longest transaction open at any point, idle ones included. It pins the vacuum horizon for as long as it runs.

spec.title: Data size
spec.description: Every database in scope added up. WAL and server log files are not counted.

spec.title: Status
spec.description: A gap is a scrape that did not reach the server; the exporter reports `pg_up` only while Alloy itself is running.

spec.title: Connections by state
spec.description: Backends across every server in scope. `idle in transaction` holds locks and pins the transaction horizon, so it blocks vacuum even while doing nothing.

spec.title: Transactions by server
spec.description: Commits and rollbacks together.

spec.name: hide_checkpoints
spec.label: Hide checkpoints
spec.description: Drop checkpoint lines from the Server log.
